Report Output Configuration Design

Status: Implemented Created: 2025-01-31 Author: Design discussion with user

Executive Summary

This document describes the design for configurable model output selection in power flow reports. The system allows models to define default outputs while enabling users to discover available outputs and override defaults at report generation time.

Core Principle: Model metadata defines available outputs and sensible defaults. Discovery APIs expose this information for both scripting and future GUI use. No persistent configuration - all preferences specified at report generation time.

Problem Statement

Users generating reports need to:

  1. Discover what outputs are available for each model type
  2. Control which outputs appear in reports (some outputs like losses are optional)
  3. Override defaults without modifying source code
  4. Support both scripting workflows (REPL/scripts) and future GUI (checkbox interfaces)

Example: Branch model computes power flows and losses, but losses should be opt-in (not shown by default).

Design Decisions

Decision 1: Default Output Flag in Model Metadata

Solution: Add default_output::Bool field to ModelObservation struct.

struct ModelObservation
    name::Symbol
    pu_type::PUType
    description::String
    units::String
    default_output::Bool  # NEW: Shown in reports by default?
end

Rationale:

  • Self-documenting: Defaults live with model definition
  • Explicit intent: Model author declares which outputs are primary vs. advanced
  • No global state: No configuration files or settings to manage
  • Backward compatible: Defaults to true (existing behavior preserved)

Example:

const BRANCH_OBSERVATIONS = [
    ModelObservation(:p_from, PowerNominal, units="pu",
                     description="Active power flow from bus i",
                     default_output=true),   # Shown by default
    ModelObservation(:p_loss, PowerNominal, units="pu",
                     description="Active power loss in branch",
                     default_output=false),  # Opt-in only
]

Decision 2: Minimal Discovery API

Solution: Provide two simple functions for discovering available outputs.

get_available_outputs(model_type) -> Vector{Symbol}  # All possible outputs
get_default_outputs(model_type) -> Vector{Symbol}    # Default subset

Rationale:

  • Minimal surface: Just two functions - easy to learn and use
  • Script-friendly: Returns simple Symbol vectors
  • Programmatic: Can be used to build UIs or validate user input
  • No metadata exposure: Users don't need to understand ModelMetadata internals

Rejected alternatives:

  • Verbose get_model_output_options() with full metadata (too complex for scripting)
  • get_checkbox_state() UI helper (premature - build when GUI exists)
  • show_available_outputs() pretty printer (users can inspect vectors directly)

Decision 3: Report-Time Configuration

Solution: Respect default_output flags when include_vars=nothing, otherwise use explicit user specification.

# In collect_model_table():
vars_to_include = if !isnothing(config.columns.include_vars)
    # User explicitly specified - use exactly what they requested
    Set{Symbol}(config.columns.include_vars)
else
    # No specification - use defaults
    default_vars = output_vars ∪ {obs.name | obs.default_output == true}
    filter(v -> v ∉ exclude_vars, default_vars)
end

Rationale:

  • No persistence needed: Configuration passed at report generation time
  • Clear precedence: Explicit include_vars overrides all defaults
  • Flexible exclusions: Can exclude specific defaults via exclude_vars
  • Stateless: No SystemModel state to manage

API Summary

Discovery Functions

# Query available outputs
julia> get_available_outputs(Branch)
[:p_from, :q_from, :p_to, :q_to, :p_loss, :q_loss]

julia> get_default_outputs(Branch)
[:p_from, :q_from, :p_to, :q_to]  # Excludes losses

Report Generation

# Default behavior - uses model defaults (no losses)
report = collect_model_table(sys, :Branch)
# Columns: I, J, Ckt, P_from (MW), Q_from (MVAR), P_to (MW), Q_to (MVAR)

# Explicitly include losses
config = ReportConfig(columns=ColumnPreferences(
    include_vars=[:p_from, :q_from, :p_loss]
))
report = collect_model_table(sys, :Branch; config=config)
# Columns: I, J, Ckt, P_from (MW), Q_from (MVAR), P_loss (MW)

# Exclude specific defaults
config = ReportConfig(columns=ColumnPreferences(
    exclude_vars=[:q_from, :q_to]
))
report = collect_model_table(sys, :Branch; config=config)
# Columns: I, J, Ckt, P_from (MW), P_to (MW)

Implementation Details

Files Modified

  1. src/foundation/core_types.jl (lines 299-322)

    • Added default_output::Bool field to ModelObservation
    • Updated constructor with default_output=true default

  2. src/powercore/reports.jl (lines 379-462, 682-702)

    • Added get_available_outputs() and get_default_outputs()
    • Updated collect_model_table() to respect default_output flags

  3. src/models/branch.jl (lines 241-284)

    • Set default_output=true for flows
    • Set default_output=false for losses

  4. All other models (PQ, PV, Bus, Shunt)

    • Added default_output=true to all existing observations (preserve existing behavior)

  5. src/powercore/PowerCore.jl and src/Powerful.jl

    • Exported get_available_outputs and get_default_outputs

Bookkeeping Structure

Model Definition (Static)
    ├─ ModelObservation with default_output flag
    │  └─ Defines available outputs and defaults
    │
Discovery API (Query)
    ├─ get_available_outputs() → All possible outputs
    └─ get_default_outputs() → Default subset

Report Generation (Runtime)
    ├─ If include_vars specified → Use explicit list
    └─ Otherwise → Use default_output flags + exclude_vars

For future GUI integration:

  • get_available_outputs() provides checkbox list
  • get_default_outputs() provides initial checkbox state
  • User selections stored as Vector{Symbol} (simple serialization)
  • Pass selections via include_vars at report generation

Future Enhancements (Not Implemented)

These features were considered but deemed unnecessary for current needs:

  1. Per-model persistent preferences - Would require config file management
  2. Pretty printer (show_available_outputs()) - Users can inspect vectors
  3. Full metadata query - Discovery APIs sufficient for current use cases
  4. UI helper functions - Premature until GUI exists

Testing

Verified behavior:

  • ✓ Branch losses excluded by default
  • ✓ Branch losses included when explicitly requested
  • ✓ Discovery APIs return correct outputs
  • ✓ Exclusions work on default variables
  • ✓ All other models preserve existing behavior (all observations shown)
